cards.explanation: The reason He gives is that the land is departing from the LORD. He says, "…because this land is flagrantly prostituting itself by departing from the LORD." (Hosea 1:2) So the reason is about the land, not about Hosea. I think that's worth a slow read, friends, because it's a heavy way to start a book.

The answer is False. The text shows Hosea going, not pushing back. It says, "So Hosea went and married Gomer daughter of Diblaim…" (Hosea 1:3) It doesn't record a single word of argument from him, friends, and I won't make one up either.

The answer is Israel. The LORD says, "…I will put an end to the kingdom of Israel." (Hosea 1:4) Jeroboam was Israel's king when this word came. Bloodshed on the house of Jehu, and an end to the kingdom, friends. Both are in the same verse.

The answer is the bow of Israel. The LORD says, "And on that day I will break the bow of Israel in the Valley of Jezreel." (Hosea 1:5) A bow is a weapon, so I think breaking it points to Israel's strength being broken. That's my guess, though, friends, because the verse itself just says what He will break.

The answer is False. The LORD says, "Yet I will have compassion on the house of Judah, and I will save them…" (Hosea 1:7) That word "Yet" is doing a lot of work, friends. Israel hears one word, and Judah hears a different one.

The answer is by the LORD their God. He says He'll save them "…not by bow or sword or war, not by horses and cavalry, but by the LORD their God." (Hosea 1:7) Notice how many things He lists that won't do it, friends. Then He names the one that will.
The answer is True. The LORD says, "Name him Lo-ammi, for you are not My people, and I am not your God." (Hosea 1:9) Those are His exact words, friends. It's a hard sentence, and I won't dress it up.
